findings.text: VM descriptor ioctl dispatcher validates that the caller address space still owns the VM and that the VM is alive, then routes requests for vcpu creation, capability enablement, memory region setup, dirty tracking, coalesced zones, eventfds, message interrupts, irq levels, routing tables, memory attributes, device creation, extension queries, ring resets, statistics and guest memory, delegating unrecognized codes to arch handling.

User memory region setup accepts two structure versions sharing a common initial layout for slot, flags, guest address, size and user address, enforced at build time; legacy submissions are zero extended and restricted to a narrower flag mask before being forwarded to a common region installer.

Generic extension query reports per-feature support levels for coalesced access, manual dirty protection, interrupt routing capacity, address space count, slot count, dirty ring sizing under different ordering options, statistics, event payloads, device control and memory features, returning neutral values when build options disable a feature and deferring unknown identifiers to arch logic.

Dirty ring sizing can be performed only once and only before any vcpu exists; the request is rejected unless an offset capability is present, the length is a binary power, it covers both reserved entries and at least a full page, and it stays within a global maximum; updates are serialized by the VM mutex.

Dirty ring reset requires a configured ring, walks all vcpus under the slot mutex resetting each per-vcpu ring while accumulating a cleared indicator, then issues a remote TLB flush when any progress was reported and returns the indicator.

Combined ring plus bitmap mode is enabled only when bitmap support is compiled in, a ring size was already established, no flags are supplied, and every address space currently holds no memory slots; the transition is guarded by the slot mutex.

Generic capability enablement validates manual dirty protection masks against allowed combinations, constrains halt polling delay to a narrow integer width before publishing it with an ordering barrier and an override marker, and gates dirty ring variants on their advertised availability before invoking shared helpers.

VM statistics are exposed through a read-only anonymous file whose operations bind read to a shared statistics formatter over the VM counters, release to a VM reference drop, and seek to a no-op; the file holds a private pointer to the owning VM.

Statistics descriptor creation reserves a close-on-exec descriptor, instantiates an anonymous inode for VM statistics in read-only pread mode, acquires an additional VM reference, installs the file and returns the descriptor, unwinding reservations on failure.

Compatibility variants of dirty log requests replicate native slot and paging fields while carrying the user bitmap as a narrowed pointer inside a union that preserves native width, allowing translation to native form by widening the pointer and copying scalar fields.

Compatibility VM ioctl handling first offers the request to arch compatibility logic and returns unless it declines, then translates compatibility dirty and clear requests into native structures before dispatching to shared handlers, otherwise falling back to the native VM dispatcher with identical liveness checks.
VM file operations expose release for teardown, native ioctl dispatch, a no-op seek, and a compatibility ioctl entry that is active only where compatibility support is configured.

Device-level VM creation reserves a descriptor, allocates a VM object named after that descriptor, wraps it in a read-write anonymous VM file, emits a creation event and installs the descriptor; failures release the VM reference and descriptor in reverse order, while success transfers lifetime to file release.

Top-level device ioctl answers API version queries only with a cleared argument, creates VMs, evaluates generic extension support without a VM context, computes vcpu mapping length as a base run structure plus optional architecture and coalesced pages, and forwards other codes to arch device handling.

The control device is registered as a miscellaneous device under the conventional virtualization name with operations limited to device ioctl dispatch, no-op seeking and shared compatibility handling.
A global flag controlling whether virtualization is enabled at module load defaults to enabled and becomes read-only after initialization.

Per-CPU virtualization state tracks enablement independently on each processor, coordinated by a global usage mutex and reference count; the architecture shutdown hook defaults to an empty weak definition.

Per-CPU enablement is idempotent and reports failure when arch enablement fails; online processing aborts if enablement fails, offline always disables, shutdown invokes arch shutdown then disables virtualization on every processor, while suspend and resume assert lock and interrupt preconditions around the same transitions and are published through system core operations.

Bus write with a caller supplied hint first validates the hint against device count and address range overlap, completing immediately on a matching device write success and otherwise falling back to a full bus search that yields the correct position.

Lookup of a device by bus and guest address requires the VM source-read lock to be held, returns absent when no bus is present or when no range matches a single byte probe, and otherwise returns the device pointer from the located range.

Bus ordering relies on a shared range comparator exposed through a sort callback, and bus teardown is deferred through a read-copy-update callback that recovers the enclosing bus object before releasing it.

Both native and compatibility VM dispatchers fail requests with an I/O error when the calling address space no longer matches the creator or when the VM has been marked dead, preventing use after release or cross-process misuse.

Routing table replacement validates architecture permission, enforces a maximum entry count and requires reserved flags to be clear, duplicating user entries only when entries exist and releasing the temporary copy after installation.
The device reports a stable API version number and defines vcpu mapping length as a base page plus optional architecture and coalesced pages.
Extension and command identifiers form a stable user ABI covering version, creation, memory, dirty tracking, interrupts, routing, statistics and device management.

Default weak handlers reject generic VM capability enablement as invalid, decline arch compatibility ioctls as inappropriate, and provide an empty arch shutdown, allowing architectures to override each hook.
Empty check over all address spaces requires the slot mutex to be held and reports true only when every per-space slot table is empty.
